result:
I fixed 12 of the 150 rules in `pricebook.py` so they now match their docstrings. I wrote a script that rebuilds each rule from its docstring and the module's shared rules, then compares it with the real function over many quantities and unit prices. After the fix, all 150 rules give the same results as their docstrings.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 13, 150 | Used `qty > N`, so the discount didn't apply at exactly the threshold | Changed to `>=` |
| 47 | Threshold was 101 instead of 100 | Changed to 100 |
| 18, 49, 84 | Used `round()`, which can round up | Changed to `//` (floor), per the shared rule |
| 42, 111 | Labelled "whole" but discounted only the units above the threshold ("marginal") | Discount now applies to all units (`base`) |
| 68 | The 50,000 cap only applied when the discount was over 100,000 | Cap now always applies |
| 69 | Capped the price at 100,000 instead of the discount | Now caps the discount, per the shared rule |
| 99 | Discount was 8% instead of 7% | Changed to 7% |
| 117 | Discount was 4% instead of 3% | Changed to 3% |

The check covered quantities 0–129, 200, 1,000 and 5,000, each with 11 unit prices from 0 to 1,000,000. It's a broad sample, not every possible input.

STATUS: DONE
